microstructure: Single-phase austenite with annealing twins; strengthened by cold work (strain-induced martensite possible in 301/304). Sensitisation risk (Cr carbides at grain boundaries) if held ~450–850 °C with higher C.
Phase balance (≈40–60% ferrite) set by chemistry + solution anneal/quench; intermetallic (sigma, chi) risk ≈600–1000 °C; 475 °C embrittlement of ferrite.
Solution-treated lath martensite; ageing (H900–H1150) precipitates Cu-rich phase — condition sets strength/toughness/SCC resistance.

crystalStructure: Tempered martensite: BCC ferrite matrix + alloy carbides (as-quenched martensite is BCT)
microstructure: Q&T gives tempered martensite/bainite; prior-austenite grain size controls toughness. Risks: temper embrittlement, quench cracking, hydrogen embrittlement at high strength.

crystalStructure: BCC α-ferrite + Fe3C (pearlite); BCT martensite if quenched
microstructure: Ferrite + pearlite (lever-rule estimate ≈44% pearlite at 0.35%C, ≈64% at 0.50%C); tempered martensite after Q&T. Hardenability is carbon-controlled (modest).

crystalStructure: BCC ferrite + pearlite/bainite; fine Nb/V/Ti carbonitride precipitates
microstructure: Fine-grained ferrite-pearlite from controlled rolling; strength from grain refinement + precipitation. Weld HAZ grain coarsening can reduce toughness.
